reading.text:
Reading for def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.IsBrownianFiltration (written before seeing any Lean).

Paper notion. Section 2: (F_t) is the usual augmentation of the filtration generated by W, N and
an independent initial sigma-field F_0, with W a d-dimensional BM independent of N. What the
Brownian stochastic integral needs, and what this setting provides, is that W is an
(F_t)-Brownian motion: (i) W_t is F_t-measurable for every t (adapted); (ii) for s <= t the
increment W_t - W_s is independent of F_s. (The filtration is not the natural filtration of W:
it also contains N and F_0; so a predicate requiring F to be generated by W would be too strong
and would exclude the paper's setting, unless the Brownian--Poisson case is formalised with a
different predicate.)

A faithful Lean predicate "IsBrownianFiltration" (relating a filtration F and a BM W) must:
- assert adaptedness of W to F and independence of future increments W_t - W_s (s <= t) from
  F_s, with respect to the reference measure P;
- be satisfiable by the paper's filtration (augmented, containing N and F_0); it should not
  require F to be the natural filtration of W or right-continuity/completeness beyond what the
  usual conditions give (usual conditions are fine);
- independence must be of the increment from the whole sigma-algebra F_s (not just from W_s).

comparison.text:
Comparison for IsBrownianFiltration.
Lean: structure (Prop) for W : BrownianMotion P and ℱ : Filtration ℝ (ambient σ-algebra):
measurable: ∀ t, W_t is ℱ_t-measurable; indep_future: ∀ s ≥ 0, ℱ_s is independent (under P) of
⨆_{t > s} σ(W_t − W_s).
- Adaptedness: yes (everywhere-measurable, for all real t).
- Independence: the whole σ-algebra ℱ_s is independent of the σ-algebra of all future increments.
  This is the (ℱ_t)-Brownian-motion property (it implies increment-by-increment independence).
  It is not merely independence from W_s. Matches.
- No requirement that ℱ be the natural filtration of W, and no completeness or right-continuity
  requirement. The paper's filtration (the usual augmentation of σ(W, N, F_0), with W, N, F_0
  independent) satisfies both fields. The future Brownian increments are independent of F_0, of
  the past of W and of the past of N. Null sets do not affect independence, and a.s.-zero W_t for
  t < 0 is measurable for an augmented ℱ_t. The filtration is indexed by ℝ, so the paper's
  [0,T]-filtration has to be extended, e.g. constantly for t < 0. That is a harmless convention.
Verdict: faithful with representation choices.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices. (1) The filtration is indexed by ℝ rather than [0,T], and adaptedness is
required for every real t. For the paper's augmented filtration, extended by F_0 for t < 0 (and
naturally for t > T), this holds, because W_t = 0 a.s. for t < 0 and the augmentation contains the
null sets. (2) Independence is stated for the σ-algebra of all future increments jointly, which is
the standard (F_t)-BM property and holds for the paper's filtration generated by independent W, N
and F_0. (3) The predicate is for one-dimensional components. The specs apply it to each
component W.W j of the d-dimensional motion, and joint independence is not part of this predicate.

author_review.disagreements: No disagreement on the substance. The author's entry (acceptance/review/definitions.md) records only the review marker, or a section heading, and no comparison with the paper. It does not state the points I relied on: the predicate is adaptedness for every real t plus independence of ℱ_s from the joint σ-algebra of all future increments. It holds for the paper's augmented filtration of independent W, N and F_0 (extended to t < 0), and it is applied per component.
